sp106box10.note: The files are a code grid (R658), a codebreaker's word list (R701), a table-decode check of 46 groups (R702) and two or three phrases from R664; not continuous prose, consistent with the 0.1 claim.

sp106r597.note: A clear-text English instruction sheet for a cipher with a worked numeric example, not a ciphered message; the file is a transcription of that sheet.

sp106r927.note: Per-line two-column table (marked decrypt | regularised French), words split across lines with hyphens; the regularised column reads as good French with only a few [..]. Needs reflowing into paragraphs and translating.

sperantio1534.note: R9415 is a normalised Latin reading with scattered '?' and <..> marks; R9412 is line-numbered German with some [..] gaps, still easy to read.

spinelly1516.note: One short cipher passage, fully read, coherent English with two bracketed guesses.

stafford1586.note: plaintext.txt is only the four cipher runs (villequier / king of navarre / kyll him and the prince of conde / duke of guise): short phrases and names, not continuous prose; the rest of the letter is in clear English.

stowe166.note: Coherent late-16th-century English, original spelling, no punctuation, lower case, code signs as {..}; short cipher passages extracted from clear letters. Needs light normalising only.

sunyatsen.note: Short telegram in clear Chinese with English translation; one garbled character and a garbled last word.

sweden4306.note: Short letter, one paragraph, fully read except a few numbered name codes; spaced Dutch with an English translation.

swieten1757.note: READING.md gives the single R955 letter as one clean French sentence (clear copy of the decipherment).

swieten1759.note: Continuous French with cipher in guillemets; unread groups are a few numbered name codes ([232 G...], [147 100 126 148], [170 271 289 337]) scattered one or two per paragraph. Some gaps (...) between passages.

szembek1689.note: Punctuated Latin prose with abbreviations expanded, cipher words italicised, one code group [202] open. Fully translatable as it stands.

throck1559.note: main_decrypt.txt decodes only lines 1-5 (the rest are bare sign transcriptions); the published running reading is clean for the first three lines, then every few words is interrupted by [...] ('to [...] knowledge of considering the present [...] to dispatch [...] gentleman'). The 85% is of signs, but a reader cannot assemble the second half into sentences.

throck1560.note: OCR of the printed Forbes 1740s edition: sixteenth-century English, coherent, but carries long-s, running heads, marginal numerals and broken line-end words.

throck1569.note: Letter in 16th-c English with clear text plain and cipher in italics; scattered [code]/[?] holes (a few per paragraph) do not stop the argument being followed.

throckmorton.note: Texts are the printed Calendar of State Papers Foreign English summaries of the despatches (not a decipherment of ours); fully coherent. Control decodes (control_reading.txt) are fragments only ('all be it i be revoked or the warr breake').

toledo1565.note: Full-letter Spanish reading in paragraphs, cipher in italics, manuscript spelling kept; no holes in the sample. no. 249 is a decode with the figure groups still unrevealed in places (e.g. '18 29 37 35 ...') in the code block, but the prose reading above it reads through.

tranchedini1452.note: lasry_entry.md holds only the report header (sender, key, element counts) and 'Plaintext available'; the excerpt and translation promised in the profile summary are not in the file, and the ciphertext is not transcribed. No decryption text is published.

transylvania1645.note: R4936 is an unspaced provisional mechanical decode with open q/g, c/p, i/n confusions: clear-text Hungarian is legible but cipher passages run as letter streams with garbled words. R4940 gives two words only. No checked reading exists (file itself says so).

turculet1709.note: Normalised Polish and Latin prose, punctuated, no holes.

turenne1528.note: Only Lasry's report excerpt (a few lines plus English translation) is in the repository; it is clean and coherent, but the full decipherment is not published here.

urquhart.note: The Octastich is a full eight-line English poem; the Distich has no decipherment (0/64), which is why the whole is only 0.785. The raw letter string reading_octastich.txt is noisy but the verse is given cleanly.

vanreede1787.note: Cipher text is a stream of fragments, stray capitals and unresolved [codes] in nearly every sentence; the clear lines are themselves OCR-like garbage in R1026. A reader cannot build the letter's sentences.

vanreede1792.note: Short cover note, fully read with French text and English translation; the nulls are declared.

vasto1527.note: Cipher runs join into coherent Spanish with lightly punctuated spacing and scattered <[xxx]> unread groups (34 of 1680 tokens); the file has a measurement header and omits clear text between runs.

vergier1696.note: Only Lasry's report excerpt (a few lines plus English translation) is in the repository; it is clean and coherent, but the full decipherment is not published here.

vetesi1705.note: The only file is a DECODE transcription of a contemporary interlinear gloss, with cipher numbers and garbled Hungarian between clear-text snippets; no sentence can be built. The reading exists only as the 1706 interlinear and Ráday edition.

vich1511.note: Per-line decoder output with broken word division (a stray space inside nearly every word), wrong letters (n/u, v/u) and [xxx] holes on most lines, worst in N.60 (L0309 'a [ree] ar de italia'). Spanish gist is recoverable with effort but sentences are not clean; 0.965 looks generous.

villardeau.note: Only a two-line excerpt of a 1,248-element, 5-page decryption is published; the full text is not in the repository. The excerpt is clean French.

villeneuve1737.note: Lasry's excerpts with translation are clean French; only excerpts are published, not the full letters.

villeroy258.note: Short excerpt with translation, coherent; full text not published here.

visconti1528.note: Line-by-line glyph table with Italian reading; most lines give readable Italian (r16-r20 flow well) with a few unresolved glyphs per page, and final.md carries a connected English-style summary. Published form is raw per-line tables with glyph tokens, not continuous prose.

visconti1529.note: Continuous Italian paragraphs with scattered (?) and [..] marks and an English summary; f28 is at 91% with more doubtful words but still builds sentences.

vizani1637.note: Short passage (54 cipher words) reads as Italian sentences with five bracketed name codes and a couple of ? words; Satoru's reading, partly with '...' elisions. The raw one-line decode in the file is unspaced and misspelt (monignor).

vulcob1573.note: Only a three-line excerpt with translation (Lasry's report) is in the repository; it reads cleanly but the full text is not published here.

walsingham1585.note: R4840 first paragraph is coherent English with name codes glossed, but later sentences carry [..] holes in most clauses; R4844 has unread sign-alphabet words in nearly every sentence. Profile 0.49 is consistent.

wardein1537.note: Early-modern German; some lines read as full clauses, but most lines carry a [..n] hole or <variant> and several sentences (P1.12-P1.32) break into fragments.

warsaw.note: Short letter; word-divided, punctuated Italian with an English working translation; about a dozen [nnn] code groups, but they are fillers/titles and the sentence is clear.

wesselenyi1664.note: Clean Latin with English translation; only the two place codes [60], [64] open.

windischgraetz1720.note: Cipher passages A-Z with clear context and a reading column are coherent German, but published as a table of numbers and key values per passage rather than a running letter.

windischgraetz1720b.note: Each passage is shown as cipher figures, letter-by-letter decoding and an English 'Reading' line; the German sentences are coherent and complete but split into passages with decoder scaffolding, and the surrounding clear text is not transcribed.

windischgraetz1721.note: German passage-by-passage output with «tentative codes» and ALL-CAPS unspaced runs (EXCVSATIONZVMACHEN); most lines have one or two code or ? gaps but the sense of each sentence is recoverable; needs normalising and translation.

yard1699.note: Punctuated English letters with deciphered words in italics; fully coherent. oct12_decoded.txt is raw syllable output but plaintext.md is clean.
